hook: The admiral of the Ming treasure fleets, who sailed to Africa long before Europe did.

pages.x: Ma He was born in 1371 in Yunnan, in south-west China, into a Muslim family; his father had made the pilgrimage to Mecca. When Ming armies conquered Yunnan, the ten-year-old was captured and sent to serve a prince, Zhu Di.

He grew tall and strong and became one of the prince's trusted commanders. When Zhu Di seized the throne in 1402 as the Yongle Emperor, he gave Ma He a new name, Zheng He, and put him in charge of a vast new fleet.

In 1405 he sailed with over 300 ships and 27,000 men. The biggest "treasure ships" may have been over 100 metres long, several times the size of any European ship of the day. Over 28 years he led seven voyages across the Indian Ocean.

His fleets visited Java, Sri Lanka, Calicut in India, Hormuz in Persia, Aden in Arabia, and Mogadishu and Malindi in East Africa. Kings sent envoys back to China with the fleet, and some came themselves.
In 1414 the fleet brought a giraffe to China. The court thought it was a qilin, a magical creature that appears only when a wise ruler is on the throne, and had its portrait painted.

Zheng He died around 1433 on his last voyage, perhaps buried at sea. Later emperors decided the voyages cost too much, and a story says an official burned their records. China turned inward just as Europeans began to sail.
Zheng He led the greatest fleets the world had seen, decades before Columbus and Vasco da Gama. He is a hero in China today, and temples in Southeast Asia honour him.
pts: Led seven great voyages across the Indian Ocean
Commanded the largest wooden fleet in history
Reached East Africa 80 years before the Portuguese
